msg: Telnet is on in the shipped default. An unencrypted remote shell in the default configuration is the textbook Art. 3(3)(d) finding; use SSH over TLS or drop the service from the image.

article: UK PSTI Regs 2023 Sch. 1 para. 1 / RED Art. 3(3)(d)
msg: Universal default password in a shipped default. PSTI Schedule 1 paragraph 1 bans passwords that are neither unique per device nor forced to change on first use; generate per unit or require a change at first boot.
Credential baked into source or config: everyone holding one firmware image holds it, so a single extraction breaks the whole fleet. Read it from a secure element or a provisioning-time variable.
MQTT without authentication or without TLS (port 1883, mqtt://, allow_anonymous). Anyone on the path can publish commands to the device; move to 8883 with TLS and per-device credentials.

article: RED Art. 3(3)(e) / EN 18031-2 (confidentiality of personal data)
msg: Certificate verification is off, so TLS here stops nothing: any proxy on the route can read and rewrite the payload. Bundle or pin a CA and leave verification on.
Update signature checking or secure boot is disabled, which makes the update channel itself the shortest attack path into the fleet. Sign images and verify before flashing.
Firmware is fetched over plain HTTP. DNS or route interference lets someone hand the device their image; use HTTPS and verify the signature after download.
The radio link ships open or on a broken cipher (open, none, WEP, TKIP). WPA2-PSK is the floor and WPA3 is the ask where the chipset allows it.
A debug interface is enabled in the shipped default. JTAG, SWD or an open console hands over memory and keys on the bench; gate it off for production builds.
Telemetry is on by default and nothing in this file records a consent or opt-in gate. EN 18031-2 expects personal-data flows to stay under user control: default it off and ask.

article: RED Art. 3(3)(e) / EN 18031-2 (confidentiality of personal data)
msg: Device data leaves over plain HTTP to a non-local host. Whatever is personal in that payload is readable on the wire; switch the endpoint to HTTPS.
An identifier or location field is written to logs. Logs get shipped, pooled and kept, so this is a personal-data flow riding along with diagnostics; hash it or drop the field.
A control interface is exposed with authentication switched off. Art. 3(3)(f) is the money limb: if a command can spend, credit or unlock, the caller has to be authenticated.

This manifest declares a product but no vulnerability-reporting contact. PSTI Schedule 1 paragraph 2 requires a published point of contact plus acknowledgement and status updates; add security_contact and the policy URL.
No defined support period in the manifest. PSTI Schedule 1 paragraph 3 requires the minimum length of time security updates will be supplied, published with the product as a date or a period.

msg_past: The published support period ended {date}, {days} days before today ({today}). The security-update statement shipped with these units is no longer true.
msg_soon: The published support period ends {date}, {days} days from today ({today}). Extend it or prepare the end-of-support notice before the date passes.

article: Harmonised standards cited for RED Art. 3(3)(d)(e)(f)
msg: EN 303 645 is the ETSI consumer-IoT baseline, not a harmonised standard under the RED delegated regulation. The cited standards for Art. 3(3)(d)(e)(f) are EN 18031-1, EN 18031-2 and EN 18031-3; 303 645 alone carries no presumption of conformity.
EN 18031 cited with no part. The parts are not interchangeable: -1 is network protection (d), -2 is personal data and privacy (e), -3 is protection from fraud (f). Name the part you tested against.
The RED cybersecurity requirements were deferred by amendment: they apply from 1 August 2025, not August 2024. A declaration or plan still carrying the old date reads as never revisited.
